examples.title: A live run keeps its actions in reach
examples.description: The bar sticks to the bottom of the scrolling area while the page scrolls behind it. It clears the home indicator and rides above the on-screen keyboard, and on touch every control is 44px.

examples.title: A decision bar with equal actions
examples.description: equalActions gives Deny and Approve the same width. Below 32rem of bar width the pair takes its own row under the consequence line and shares it.

examples.title: Off together, with the reason
examples.description: While the stream is reconnecting the bar is off. Buttons that opt in with mutating stay focusable and are described by the reason, which is drawn under the row and announced politely. The field is read-only.
examples.code:
<script lang="ts">
  import { Button, DockedActionBar, Input } from '@lostgradient/cinder';

  let off = $state(true);
  let message = $state('');
</script>

<DockedActionBar
  label="Run actions"
  {off}
  reason="Reconnecting… Send a message and Cancel run are off until the connection is back."
>
  <Input
    id="run-context-off"
    bind:value={message}
    label="Add context"
    labelVisible={false}
    placeholder="Add context the agent will see on its next step"
    readonly={off}
  />
  {#snippet actions()}
    <Button mutating variant="secondary">Send a message</Button>
    <Button mutating variant="secondary">Cancel run</Button>
    <Button variant="ghost" onclick={() => (off = !off)}
      >{off ? 'Reconnect' : 'Drop the stream'}</Button
    >
  {/snippet}
</DockedActionBar>
